subject: Discovery Recap: tool calling & structured output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@acmehealth.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: tool calling & structured output requirements

Hi Sana / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — great first conversation. Below is a short recap so we have shared expectations and clear next steps. Please correct anything I've missed.

1) Pain points (what keeps you up at night)
- Inconsistent structured outputs from current agents leading to downstream parsing errors in your clinical workflow automation.
- Difficulty guaranteeing deterministic JSON formatting (schemas and ordering) when invoking 3rd-party tools.
- High latency during multi-step agent workflows when hitting external tool endpoints.

2) Current stack
- Orchestration: internal Python-based agent runner (homegrown)
- Model hosts: mix of hosted Llama variants + a managed OpenAI endpoint for fallback
- Tooling: HTTP webhooks for EHR/tool calls, Lambda for small fns, DB: Postgres

3) Success criteria (how Acme Health will measure success)
- Deterministic JSON outputs that validate against a provided JSON Schema > 99% of the time for core patient-summary workflows.
- End-to-end median latency <= 600ms for single-tool calls and <= 1.8s for 3-step agent flows at typical load.
- Clear audit trail for tool calls (request/response + model decisions) for SOC/clinical review.

4) Specifics on tool & structured output needs discussed
- You need function/tool calling support where model responses map to a strict JSON Schema (fields, types, enums, and required ordering for your parsers).
- Want ability to reject or flag model outputs that deviate from schema instead of trying to patch in downstream code.
- Agent workflows include: 1) gather patient context -> 2) call clinical-rules-tool -> 3) format structured summary -> 4) store + trigger downstream workflow.

5) Next steps (agreed)
- Redwood to provide: sample JSON Schema and a suggested deterministic formatting profile (we attached a draft sample).
- Schedule technical deep-dive with your engineering team and our SE (Ava) to run through agent wiring, schema validation, and latency tuning. Proposed windows next Tue/Wed morning PT.
- Share example datasets (anonymized) so we can run a quick eval against the schema and measure pass-rate.

Attachments: MAP-AcmeHealth-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan with timeline), rdw-sample-json-schema.md (example schema + formatting notes).

If that all looks correct, I can book the SE deep-dive for Tuesday 10 AM PT and initial eval runs the same week.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0162

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap, this matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications: 

- Deterministic formatting: when you say "ordering", do you mean we require a strict key order in JSON (we rely on positional parsing in one legacy piece) or is validating presence/types/enums sufficient for now?
- Datasets: we'll send a small anonymized sample (10-15 records) by end of day Friday.

We prefer Tue 10 AM PT for the SE deep-dive. I'll invite our lead eng (Tom) and the clinical data owner.

One ask: can Redwood's validation step be configured to return a machine-friendly error object when schema validation fails (so we can automate retries)? That would help our pipeline.

Best,
Sana Patel
Director, Clinical Automation | Acme Health
sana.patel@acmehealth.com | (617) 555-0199

Thanks for the quick replies & the confirmation, Sana — a few answers inline: 

- Key ordering: we recommend you avoid relying on key order where possible, but we can support a deterministic serializer that enforces a canonical order for downstream parsers. We discussed two modes: (1) schema-validation-only (presence/types/enums) with a rich error object, and (2) schema + canonical ordering enforced in the generation path. We can demo both.

- Machine-friendly errors: yes, Redwood can return a structured validation error object with an error code, failing_field_paths, and suggested remediation hints. That integrates with your retry logic.

I'll go ahead and book Tuesday 10 AM PT for the technical deep-dive and include Ava as the Redwood SE. Calendar invite + Miro/Zoom link to follow.

Next immediate action: we'll run the anonymized sample through a quick schema pass and share results in 48 hours (TBD based on when you send the sample).

Jordan
